replacement: In the end the elder’s death came quite unexpectedly. The people gathered around him that last evening knew that his death was near. Still, it was hard to imagine it would come so suddenly. On the contrary, as I said before, his friends saw him that night apparently so cheerful and talkative that they were convinced his condition had changed for the better, at least for a time. Even five minutes before he died, they said afterwards in amazement, there was no way of foreseeing it. He seemed suddenly to feel a sharp pain in his chest. He went pale and pressed his hands to his heart. Everyone got up from their seats and hurried to him. But though he was in pain, he still looked at them with a smile. He slid slowly from his chair to his knees, then bowed his face to the ground, stretched out his arms, and, as if in joyful ecstasy, praying and kissing the ground, he quietly and joyfully gave up his soul to God.
The Pole gasped with offended dignity and quickly and pompously said in broken Russian:

Mihail Makarovitch was not very efficient at his work, though he did it no worse than many others. To put it plainly, he was a man of rather limited education. He could not always be trusted to know where his official powers ended. He didn’t exactly fail to understand certain reforms of the present reign. Rather, he made glaring blunders when he applied them. This wasn’t because he was especially dull. He was careless, and always too hurried to look into the matter properly.
“Forget the pestle!” burst from him suddenly.
“Confound his sorrow! Well, where to now? Do I just go on sitting here?”

“Yes, I see a vital difference! Any man can be a scoundrel, and perhaps every man is one, but not everyone can be a thief. For that you have to be an arch-scoundrel. Oh, of course, I don’t know how to draw these fine lines ... but a thief is lower than a scoundrel, that’s what I believe. Listen: I carry the money on me for a whole month. I might make up my mind tomorrow to give it back, and then I’m not a scoundrel anymore. But I can’t make up my mind, you see, though I decide every day, every day I push myself to do it, and still for a whole month I can’t bring myself to it. Is that right, do you think? Is that right?”
